The deployment process requires careful coordination across multiple teams. First, prepare the release package by collecting all approved changes and building the artifact. Next, configure the target environment with the necessary credentials and permissions. The validation stage runs automated tests against the staging environment to catch issues early. Once validation passes, execute the cutover plan which involves stopping the old service, starting the new version, and monitoring health checks. Finally, document all changes and alert stakeholders about the new features available to users. The entire cycle typically requires four hours of preparation work before the actual deployment begins. Network configuration must be verified to ensure connectivity works as expected. Teams should prepare rollback procedures in case unexpected issues emerge during the deployment. Post-deployment analysis captures metrics about system performance and customer usage patterns.
